body.statement: For every \(0<\rho<1\), the exact worst-instance multiplier within \(\mathfrak D_2\) is \[\inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\frac{\Gamma_{\rho,w}(\mu)}{I_w(\mu)}=\min\left\{\rho C,\ 1+(1-\rho)\eta\right\}.\] A best-elimination witness with \(h\in\arg\min_k C_k\) attains the first branch. For an \(e\in\arg\min_k w_k/(1-w_k)\), two distinct survivors and a sufficiently separated eliminated arm attain the second branch. Consequently \(\rho^\star\) uniquely maximizes the displayed value and the maximum is \(G\).
body.justification: This theorem remains the exact eliminate-one reduction of the stronger survivor-count frontier.
body.gap: The broader top-\(m\) theorem closes the former material maximality gap while preserving the original result as \(m=K-1\).
body.consumer: Existing eliminate-one implementations retain the original optimal schedule and matching witnesses.
body.proof_tex:
Apply \(\text{thm:multi-proportional-frontier}\) with \(m=K-1\) and \(\ell=1\). The specialization identities proved there give
\[
 \mathsf D_{\rho,w,K-1}=\mathsf D_{\rho,w},\qquad
 \Gamma_{\rho,w,K-1}=\Gamma_{\rho,w},\qquad
 C_{K-1}=C,
\]
and
\[
 \eta_1=\frac{\min_e w_e}{1-\min_e w_e}
 =\min_e\frac{w_e}{1-w_e}=\eta.
\]
The exact value (22) therefore becomes
\[
 \inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\frac{\Gamma_{\rho,w}(\mu)}{I_w(\mu)}
 =\min\{\rho C,1+(1-\rho)\eta\}.
\]
The best-exclusion construction has \(S=\mathcal A\setminus\{h\}\) and is exactly the stated best-elimination witness. The separated terminal construction has the singleton excluded set \(\{e\}\) with \(e\in\arg\min_k w_k/(1-w_k)\), and it supplies the stated two-survivor comparison while all other survivor means are separated. Finally the intersection and strict monotonicity calculation in the same theorem gives the unique optimizer
\[
 \rho^\star=\frac{1+\eta}{C+\eta}
\]
and value \(C\rho^\star=G\), proving every assertion.
